proposals.before: Empress Jia secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter the crown prince: "Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?"
proposals.after: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
proposals.reason: The empress’s envy of the prince’s reputation, the explicit motive for the covert instructions, is omitted. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'
proposals.after: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
proposals.reason: The continuing agents are the eunuchs secretly instructed in s0015, confirmed by their continued plural advice in s0017. Both fields introduce the empress as the observer and speaker. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: He staged pony-cart wrecks for amusement.
proposals.after: He loved low carts and ponies, ordering attendants to gallop them, cutting cheek-straps and cheek-pieces so riders fell for sport.
proposals.reason: Cutting the harness/reins so the attendants fall is replaced by a general report of wrecks. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Yet he ran a palace bazaar—himself butchering, selling ale, and weighing coin.
proposals.after: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.
proposals.reason: 使人 assigns butchering and wine-selling to other people; 手揣斤兩 is the prince estimating weights by hand, not weighing coins. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: His mother's trade drew him to the stall.
proposals.after: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.
proposals.reason: The source says his mother came from a butcher family; it does not say she herself practiced the trade. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: He drew double stipends to bankroll favorites.
proposals.after: The Eastern Palace normally received five hundred thousand cash a month for all its expenses; he habitually drew two months in advance to provide for his favorites.
proposals.reason: 探取二月 describes advance drawing on two months of the existing allowance, not an increase to a double stipend. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Du Xi warned Yu to cultivate virtue—Jia was not his mother.
proposals.after: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
proposals.reason: Du Xi’s concern that Yu is not Jia’s child and that she is violent, together with the specific advice to avoid slander, is lost. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Yu pinned needles into Du Xi's seat cushion.
proposals.after: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.
proposals.reason: 使人 means he ordered someone to put needles there, whereas the idiomatic assigns the manual act to Yu. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
proposals.after: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
proposals.reason: 成都 is the principality; 穎 is the prince’s personal name. "Prince Chengdu of Ying" reverses their roles. The rest of the sentence can remain. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: And I secretly hear him say: After the empress dies I will butcher her like fish on the block.
proposals.after: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."
proposals.reason: 之 cannot refer to the empress whom the same clause has already stipulated will be dead. The threat is against the surviving Jia referent(s), conservatively left as them rather than expanded into a particular membership list. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: He warned Yu would purge Jia kin like the Yang coup.
proposals.after: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
proposals.reason: The warning about the emperor’s death, Yu’s accession, ministers’ execution and the empress’s deposition at Jinyong is reduced to an unspecified purge. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: The text read: 'Your Majesty should settle matters himself.
proposals.after: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
proposals.reason: 自了 is a demand to end one’s life in this threatening sequence, not to settle unspecified matters. The idiomatic also substitutes Father for the actual address Your Majesty. Author independently checked the full Chinese context; this remains an unapproved proposal.

proposals.before: Heaven blesses our coup—crown Daowen, empower Lady Jiang.
